clue.text: Foundation given order to accept brother? Simple to refuse pressure

indicators.note: to accept means the word for order takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: to order someone is to instruct them
Fra is the title of an Italian friar, a brother

indicators.note: to refuse means the word for simple turns away, so loses, the letter for pressure

parts.note: simple means pure, as in pure and simple

explanation.surface: A monastic foundation is told to take in a brother, but an unsophisticated one balks at the pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foundation' suggests a charity or institution, but it means the underlying framework. 'given' is a link word; 'to accept' and 'to refuse' are the container and removal signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrastructure is the basic underlying framework of a system, its foundation.

clue.text: Indistinguishable products in the same delivery?

definitions.text: Indistinguishable products in the same delivery?

parts.words: Indistinguishable products in the same delivery?
parts.note: the delivery is a birth, not a parcel, and the products are two babies so alike nobody can tell them apart

explanation.surface: Two items in one shipment that look exactly the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Siblings from a single split egg, born together and looking exactly alike, fit the clue's description.

clue.text: General's just taking a message

parts.note: just means fair, as in a just ruling
a fax is a message sent by facsimile machine

explanation.surface: A general who is fair-minded takes delivery of a dispatch.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Fairfax commanded the Parliamentary army in the English Civil War. 'taking' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairfax was a famous Parliamentary general of the English Civil War, so the name is that of a general.

clue.text: Friendship always in evidence around US university

indicators.note: around means the word for always is placed on both sides of the university

parts.note: ay (also aye) is an old word for always, ever
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Goodwill is always on show around an American campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in evidence' is padding that makes the surface read; 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is peaceful friendly relations, a synonym for friendship.

clue.text: It's still like Othello's mind before Iago's treachery

definitions.text: It's still like Othello's mind before Iago's treachery

parts.words: It's still like Othello's mind before Iago's treachery
parts.note: Othello was calm and untroubled before Iago planted his jealousy, and the word wanted also means still or motionless

explanation.surface: A remark about Shakespeare's Moor being at peace before he was deceived.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Othello, Iago tricks Othello into believing his wife unfaithful, destroying his peace of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranquil means calm and undisturbed, which is both still and how Othello's mind was before the deception.

clue.text: In Paris, an archdeacon? That's odd

parts.note: une is the French feminine form of a or an
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: Someone finds a French archdeacon a curious thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The French feminine article UNE gives the first three letters; an archdeacon's title, the Venerable, is shortened to VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven numbers are odd ones, so the word answers an exclamation about oddness.

clue.text: Without question, new route is a gem!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the anagram goes round the abbreviation
new means the letters of route is are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asked nothing, someone declares a fresh path to be a treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROUTE IS into TUROISE, and 'Without' (meaning outside) puts it around QU. 'is' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Turquoise is a blue-green semi-precious stone, a kind of gem.

clue.text: Plant producing paper with limited value

parts.note: a rag is slang for a newspaper

indicators.note: limited means the word for value is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: worth means value

explanation.surface: A plant that makes paper of little worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' docks WORTH to WORT. Ragwort is a yellow-flowered weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a common yellow-flowered weed, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Pass over the reason, somehow, to make solemn pledge

parts.note: to pass over a road or river is to cross it

indicators.note: somehow means the letters of the reason are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone skips the explanation and swears an oath anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges THE REASON into ONESHEART. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To promise solemnly that one is telling the truth is to swear by this childhood gesture.

clue.text: Remove cream —— bird's got into it

indicators.note: got into means the bird has entered the word for cream

parts.note: the cream of a group is its elite
mina, a variant of myna, is an Asian starling; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: Someone must get rid of the cream because a bird has got into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got into' signals the container; 'it' refers back to the cream, tying the two halves of the sentence together.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to get rid of it, to remove it.

clue.text: Ackroyd's acknowledgement of message received?

definitions.meaning: Agatha Christie's The Murder of ... Ackroyd gives the murdered man's first name
in radio procedure the word means message received and understood

explanation.definitionFit: Roger is Ackroyd's Christian name in the Christie novel and also the radio word for received.

clue.text: Crested tits untiringly feed their young from the first

indicators.note: from the first means the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Birds with crests work tirelessly to feed their chicks.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the initials of 'tits untiringly feed their young' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tufty means having tufts, like a crest of feathers sticking up on a bird's head.

clue.text: Peevish query about inducement university's offered

parts.note: Qu is an abbreviation for query or question

indicators.note: about means the word for inducement is turned round

parts.note: a lure is an inducement or enticement
OU is the Open University, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: An irritable question about what bribe a college is offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LURE into ERUL. 'offered' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Querulous means complaining in a petulant, whining way, which is peevish.

clue.text: During a row one looks the other way

definitions.text: During a row one looks the other way

parts.words: During a row one looks the other way
parts.note: the row is with oars, not a quarrel: the steersman of a racing boat faces forward while the rowers face backwards

explanation.surface: Someone avoids taking sides during an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The steerer of a rowing boat faces the bow while the crew face the stern, so faces the other way.

clue.text: TV doctor takes the continental breakfast -— it's so healthy

parts.note: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC television series
le is French for the
breakfast is a meal

explanation.surface: A television doctor enjoys a European-style breakfast and praises how good it is for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'it's so' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal flour keeps the whole grain and is promoted as the healthy choice.

clue.text: Small restaurant in Penman Street?

indicators.note: in means the street abbreviation goes inside the word for penman

parts.note: Laszlo Biro was the man behind the ballpoint pen, so a penman

explanation.surface: A small eatery to be found on a road named Penman Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penman Street' looks like an address; the penman is the Hungarian inventor of the ballpoint, whose name became a brand. 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant.

clue.text: Prevailing ideas an economist put in books

indicators.note: put in means the books go inside the economist's name

parts.note: John Maynard Keynes was a famous British economist
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: An economist's main themes are written up in books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' is the container signal; the books are the biblical ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Keynotes are central themes or governing ideas, those that prevail.

clue.text: Island lake to which member of family and myself returned

indicators.note: returned means the family member and myself are read backwards together

parts.note: a son is a member of a family
me is the speaker referring to themself

explanation.surface: An island lake to which a relative and the speaker came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses the family member and myself together, giving EMNOS. Lemnos is a Greek island in the Aegean.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemnos is a Greek island in the northern Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Stork creating damage endlessly here and there

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: endlessly means the phrase for here and there loses its last letter

parts.note: about means here and there, scattered around

explanation.surface: A stork is causing harm all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ABOUT to ABOU. 'creating' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The marabou is a large African stork.

clue.text: Move new folk into tower, accepting work by engineers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's engineering corps

indicators.note: accepting means the tower takes the work inside it

parts.note: a pele or peel is a small fortified tower in the Scottish borders
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone moves newcomers into a tower that houses a piece of engineering work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' is the container signal and 'by' places the engineers alongside; pele towers are found on the Anglo-Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeople a place is to fill it with inhabitants again, to move new folk in.

clue.text: It's been abolished, not having made much of a mark

definitions.text: It's been abolished, not having made much of a mark

parts.words: It's been abolished, not having made much of a mark
parts.note: the mark is the German currency, of which this coin was a hundredth part, before both were replaced by the euro

explanation.surface: Something scrapped because it never had much impact.
explanation.definitionFit: The coin was a hundredth of a German mark, withdrawn when the euro arrived.

clue.text: Round left in gun is hot

indicators.note: in means the round and left go inside the gun

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A round left in a gun is still hot from firing.
explanation.walkthrough: O and L go inside STEN. 'Hot' is slang for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen, as in hot goods.

clue.text: Rotten argument over food sent to quarters

indicators.note: over means the word for argument is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a row is an argument
meat is food
E and N, east and north, are compass quarters

explanation.surface: A rotten row over food being sent to soldiers' billets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses ROW to WOR. 'sent to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Worm-eaten wood or fruit is decayed and riddled, rotten.

clue.text: Tree in the Strand, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is pronounced and replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a strand is a beach or shore

explanation.surface: A tree growing in the Strand, the London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London street, but here strand means shore. 'in the' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The beech is a common broadleaf tree.

clue.text: Monster originally recorded in Scottish island

indicators.note: in means the first letter of recorded goes inside the island

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of recorded is used

explanation.surface: A monster first sighted on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside BUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a savage, cruel creature, a monster.

clue.text: Magnificent old coin

definitions.meaning: magnificent here means grand and imposing in appearance
an old English gold coin worth a third of a pound

explanation.definitionFit: Noble means grand and stately, and a noble was a gold coin of medieval England.

clue.text: Unfinished hut in abandoned Italian land

indicators.note: in means the cut hut goes inside the rearranged letters
abandoned means the letters of Italian run wild into a new order
unfinished means the word hut loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An incomplete hut in a land the Italians have deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges the Italian letters into LITANIA; 'Unfinished' cuts the hut to HU, and 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is a Baltic country, a land.

clue.text: Don't skive —- attract figures with influence

parts.note: to pull is to attract
ones are figures, numbers
weight means influence, as in carrying weight

explanation.surface: An order not to slack, and to draw in influential people.
explanation.walkthrough: To skive is British slang for dodging work.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's fair share of the work is the opposite of skiving.
